incidents.victim: CyberLogitec customers — 40+ maritime shipping and port companies
incidents.vector: Ransomware group n0n compromised South Korean maritime IT provider CyberLogitec and pivoted into the networks of its customers.
incidents.impact: Over 40 port authorities, shipping companies, and maritime operators across 18 countries had data stolen and leaked on n0n's dark web site; the group is demanding a combined $1.2 billion in ransom, making this the largest attack on the maritime sector since NotPetya in 2016.

incidents.victim: Organizations running PHP (global); confirmed compromise of a European government agency
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via two critical PHP core memory-corruption flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed PHP2Shell), exploitable before any application code runs.
incidents.impact: Millions of exploitation attempts have hit PHP-based sites worldwide (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, Magento); Unit 42 confirmed an agentic AI-driven attacker fully compromised a European government agency, stealing password hashes and MFA secrets and attempting Domain Admin escalation within two hours of exploitation.

incidents.vector: Attackers used stolen maintainer GitHub credentials to push a malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 release to PyPI and Docker Hub; the package ran a credential-stealing payload automatically via Python startup hooks, requiring no import of LiteLLM.
incidents.impact: The malware harvested developer, cloud, AI-provider, SSH, and browser credentials across any environment that started Python with the package installed, including CI/CD agents and production gateways; this is the project's second supply-chain compromise in 2026.

incidents.vector: Hacking group FulcrumSec breached TiDB Cloud backend systems and maintained access for nearly a month.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed CRM customer data, Jira tickets, source code, and service analytics between September 9 and October 7, 2026.

incidents.vector: Unspecified compromise affecting Capcom's customer account systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 11.7 million gamers was stolen, including usernames, emails, and account technical details.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach of the South Korean coffee and tea chain's customer systems.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to 2.76 million customers was stolen.

incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack against the German company's North American food services division.
incidents.impact: Food delivery services were disrupted across North America.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Quanum Lab Services Manager, the customer-facing system used to place test orders and retrieve results; unrelated to the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.
incidents.impact: Quest believes some patient data was accessed; the system was taken offline during the investigation at a company that serves roughly one in three American adults annually.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached cloud provider Railway.com and stole encrypted environment variables from customer accounts, decrypting some to obtain API keys and credentials.
incidents.impact: Customer API keys and credentials were potentially exposed; Railway believes the incident is part of a broader wave of attacks targeting AI providers and has notified affected customers to revoke keys.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach, likely of a peripheral data-handling system rather than core banking systems; data later posted to BreachForums by an actor using the handle "Siriusim."
incidents.impact: Customer PII — including KYC documentation, loan applications, and account details — for roughly 3,897 customers was leaked, drawn from a dataset of 375,000 rows and 2,722 PDF files.

incidents.victim: eMudhra and organizations relying on its certificates
incidents.vector: A flawed key-generation process at Indian certificate authority eMudhra produced eight intermediate CA private keys with only single- to double-digit bits of entropy instead of 384, making the keys trivially recoverable from the public certificates.
incidents.impact: Attackers able to derive the private keys could forge trusted TLS or code-signing certificates and intercept or impersonate affected domains; browser vendors have blocked the six TLS certificates and Microsoft has blocked the two code-signing certificates, though non-browser trust stores (VPNs, CI/CD, embedded devices) remain exposed pending updates.

incidents.vector: Breach of the Japanese securities firm's Tradeworks internet trading system.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to nearly 5,000 traders was accessed, and attackers placed unauthorized — apparently test — purchase orders on at least seven accounts.

incidents.vector: A hacker breached the Japanese VPS provider and installed malware across its Desktop Cloud server fleet, seeking credentials for trading and securities tools.
incidents.impact: Malware was installed on more than 26,700 servers before Onamae shut down all affected systems within a day of detection.

incidents.vector: Unspecified data breach disclosed by the Canadian supermarket chain.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen and affected customers were notified.

incidents.victim: Government organizations across Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Russia, and Belarus
incidents.vector: Macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE PowerShell downloaders, GitHub-hosted scripts, and a WinRAR exploit (CVE-2025-8088) delivered custom reverse shells to compromise diplomatic, economic, and environmental government entities.
incidents.impact: At least eight campaigns across Central Asia and the CIS since January 2025 targeted diplomatic negotiations, water/energy resource management, and economic ministries; operational security lapses exposed tooling suggesting the group is preparing to expand into Linux hosts and internet-facing appliances.

incidents.vector: A threat actor tracked as TAG-217 used the open-source AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX, along with several commercial AI models, to opportunistically test and exploit weaknesses across multiple financial institutions, routing traffic through residential proxies.
incidents.impact: South Korea's Financial Services Commission disclosed breaches at seven-plus financial institutions exposing personal data of at least 68,000 people; investigators also found the actor had assembled cryptocurrency-wallet theft tools and mobile-exploitation capabilities beyond the disclosed banking campaign.
